title: New research: Working adults understand hormonal health but rarely recognize it in themselves
summary: Carrot’s hormonal health report surveyed 2,000 working adults. Most understand the hormonal-metabolic link but rarely see it in themselves.
body_markdown:
Carrot’s fifth annual hormonal health report,[The Hormonal Health Gap](https://www.get-carrot.com/library/the-hormonal-health-gap) , finds that most working adults already understand how hormonal changes affect metabolic health. Far fewer connect that understanding to their own fatigue and poor sleep, which they more often attribute to stress or aging.


The report draws on an Ipsos survey of 2,000 employed, insured U.S. adults ages 35-64 (964 women and 1,036 men), fielded in September 2026. Our previous reports in[2024](https://www.get-carrot.com/blog/menopause-in-the-workplace-2024-a-report-from-carrot-fertility) and[2025](https://www.get-carrot.com/blog/the-menopause-report-2025-trends-and-statistics) focused on menopause, but this is the first Carrot hormonal health report to include men.


Key survey findings include:


- While 78% of women and 86% of men see a connection between hormonal and metabolic health, only 41% of women and 37% of men link their own symptoms to hormonal changes.
- 52% of women and 64% of men ages 35-44 blame stress for their symptoms. By ages 55-64, 46% of women and 67% of men blame normal aging.
- 57% of women and 60% of men said they’d made or considered a work-related change because of hormonal symptoms, from taking time off to leaving the workforce entirely.
- Only 45% of women and 56% of men feel supported by their employer in managing hormonal symptoms. When support is present, 78% of women and 82% of men view their employer more positively.
